item.title: 'Go to Pakistan': Dipke on those doing Hindu-Muslim 'divisive' politics
item.description: Abhijeet Dipke led a large protest in Mumbai demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Thousands of supporters gathered at Shivaji Park, despite police denying permission for the event. The Cockroach Janta Party aims to address electoral roll irregularities and the Election Commission's functioning. Dipke emphasized the importance of Hindu-Muslim unity during his speech at the protest.
item.dc:creator: HADI KHAN

item.title: Security lapse Israel overlooked? Over 12 Omani pilots flew to Tel Aviv despite ban
item.description: Israeli passengers, the captain and other pilots on board intervened, allowing the plane to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Most of the passengers were Israeli and were later flown from Saudi Arabia to Israel. Oman does not have diplomatic relations with Israel. According to the report, rules introduced after 2020 Abraham Accords prohibit pilots from countries that do not have relations with Israel from flying into the country.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Watch: Hindu temple in US attacked with bricks, windows shattered
item.description: An attack on the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights occurred while devotees were present. The incident involved bricks being thrown at the temple, resulting in shattered windows. Surveillance footage is being reviewed by authorities to identify the perpetrator. This potential hate crime coincides with Hindu Heritage Month and upcoming Navratri celebrations.
item.dc:creator: KANCHAN YADAV

item.title: China tells families of AI executives to get permission before travelling abroad
item.description: China is implementing expanded travel restrictions on senior professionals in the AI and semiconductor sectors. Family members, including spouses and children, may now require government approval for overseas travel. These measures aim to prevent the outflow of sensitive technology, information, and talent. The restrictions specifically target private-sector talent critical to China's technological ambitions. This policy reflects wider concerns over losing important expertise to other countries during global competition.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Woman stripped, assaulted at Guwahati club; manager detained
item.description: A disturbing event unfolded at a nightclub in Khanapara, Guwahati, where a woman was assaulted and stripped. The club manager has been taken in for questioning regarding the incident. Several witnesses alleged that bouncers participated in the assault and saw the attack firsthand. A video on social media depicts the victim being abused by two women as others stood by.
item.dc:creator: MUKUT DAS

item.dc:creator: PRISHA PATNAIK

item.title: Watch: Russia’s drone war machine on show as Putin watches massive military drills
item.description: Russia conducted its Center 2026 military exercise to bolster its defense strategies against potential threats. This extensive operation saw participation from approximately 47,000 troops deployed across diverse terrains, including the Caspian Sea. The drills showcased over 600 drones, 700 units of military equipment, and 60 advanced robotic systems, with allied nations like China, Belarus, and Pakistan joining the efforts.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: 'Cockroaches' from across India to march to Delhi on Oct 10, says Dipke
item.description: The Cockroach Janta Party organized a large protest in Mumbai, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke announced plans for a follow-up protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10. They accuse the Election Commission of manipulating voter rolls, affecting numerous constituencies across India. Veteran actors and students participated in the demonstration supporting the CJP's cause.
item.dc:creator: HADI KHAN

item.title: Toxic capsules, 50kg rat poison': How Pune man planned to poison 15,000 people in Mumbai
item.description: Fayyaz Premji was arrested for attempting to poison 15,000 people during a Moharrum procession in Mumbai. He ordered over 50 kg of toxic zinc phosphide and assembled capsules while staying at a lodge. The police detained him during the procession after he allegedly distributed these capsules. Preliminary evaluations suggest that the capsules contained zinc phosphide, while a forensic report is pending.
item.dc:creator: MATEEN HAFEEZ

item.title: MacKenzie Scott gave $30m to housing nonprofit; a year later, it unveiled 10-year plan
item.description: In October 2024, MacKenzie Scott made headlines by donating $30 million to Housing Trust Silicon Valley via her Yield Giving fund. This substantial contribution will support various housing initiatives over the next decade, particularly focusing on enhancing homeownership assistance. Housing Trust has a successful track record, having already developed thousands of affordable homes in the Bay Area.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: World’s richest woman Alice Walton builds a $250 million tuition-free medical school
item.description: Alice Walton’s fortune remains closely tied to her family’s Walmart holdings, while her public work has increasingly focused on art, medicine and philanthropy. Forbes estimated her wealth at nearly $120 billion in March 2026. Outside Walmart, she has committed $250 million to a medical school and $350 million toward a new healthcare campus in Bentonville.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Dalit woman ‘denied’ hospital admission over caste, gives birth by UP roadside
item.description: A 20-year-old woman from the Dalit Mushar community faced denial of admission at a government hospital in Uttar Pradesh. After being refused care due to her caste, she gave birth on the roadside with family assistance. The incident prompted immediate disciplinary action against the medical staff involved in her case. A four-member inquiry panel found negligence from multiple hospital personnel regarding her treatment.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: UPI transactions rise 27% to 145 billion in H1 FY27 ahead of new MDR
item.description: UPI has recorded significant transaction growth, processing 145 billion transactions in the first half of the financial year. The value of these transactions increased to Rs 177 lakh crore, reflecting a notable rise. A new merchant discount rate will be introduced on October 15, applying to high-value UPI transactions. Most everyday merchant transactions will remain free, with certain services facing a flat fee structure.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Maha govt took non-confrontational approach to avoid CJP stir getting bigger: Officials
item.description: In a remarkable display of solidarity, the Cockroach Janta Party's protest at Shivaji Park drew approximately 10,000 participants. The event, which was marred by a lack of official sanction from local authorities, proceeded peacefully as Mumbai police effectively controlled the crowd, much to the appreciation of protest leader Abhijeet Dipke.
item.dc:creator: CHAITANYA MARPAKWAR

item.title: Warring out, Pargat in: Has Congress solved Punjab crisis or set stage for another twist?
item.description: Amarinder Singh Raja Warring has officially resigned as the president of Punjab Congress after more than four years in leadership, a decision that follows consultations with Rahul Gandhi concerning the party's circumstances in the state. As internal strife persists, Pargat Singh has been appointed as the new leader, reflecting the ongoing factional disputes. This change poses questions about the future unity and direction of Punjab Congress amidst its turbulent dynamics.
item.dc:creator: PRIYANKA MUKHERJEE

item.title: G7’s 100-million-barrel diesel fix: What happens after the emergency release
item.description: The G7 announced an urgent release of 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products to counteract the ongoing diesel shortages, starting now and extending over the upcoming four months. Yet, experts warn that this withdrawal from emergency reserves could jeopardize future preparedness. Additionally, with supply routes still facing disruptions from geopolitical issues, the overall impact on fuel pricing and market dynamics remains ambiguous.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: No-handshake policy continues as Iyer, Farhan skip handshake at Asian Games final
item.description: Shreyas Iyer and Sahibzada Farhan maintained their no-handshake practice at the toss for the final match. This tradition has been ongoing since the 2025 Asia Cup, reflecting the tensions between India and Pakistan. India won the toss and decided to bat first in this crucial gold-medal game. India's lineup remained unchanged, featuring young Vaibhav Sooryavanshi at the top alongside Abhishek Sharma.
item.dc:creator: PRANAV SHUKLA

item.title: Women in Munich Oktoberfest given free shorts to prevent upskirting
item.description: At least 32,000 videos featuring women on the Teufelsrad have been circulated, according to Munich daily Süddeutsche Zeitung. Some have apparently been watched millions of times. The videos often show women wearing traditional dirndl dresses with their underwear visible. Some images have also been digitally manipulated to make the women appear naked, according to BR.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Brittany Mahomes supports KC Pet Project with $10,000 donation and dog adoption drive
item.description: Brittany Mahomes has supported KC Pet Project, which currently struggles with an overwhelming number of dogs. The shelter has only two open kennels while receiving a high influx of new animals daily. Recently, Brittany shared the shelter's urgent message on social media to encourage adoptions and fostering. Her family's history of support includes donations and community events promoting responsible pet ownership.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Travis Kelce, Patrick Mahomes' 1587 restaurant lawsuit takes new turn
item.description: Amid ongoing trademark issues, Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes are throwing their weight behind 1587 Prime, which has just garnered a spot on Yelp's list of Best New Restaurants for 2026. The dispute involves trademark claims from 1587 Sneakers, alleging infringement concerning their sneaker line. Seeking to distance the athletes from the legal matter, their lawyers are taking action while 1587 Prime thrives amid the conflict.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Saudi Arabia prepares for offensive against Houthis; Mecca pact allies still missing
item.description: Saudi Arabia is gearing up for a significant military campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthi forces in Yemen. This operation seeks to reclaim vital coastal territories and ensure safe maritime passage. With the potential mobilization of over 100,000 Yemeni soldiers, the success and scale of the offensive depend on overcoming ongoing challenges in uniting these troops.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Salman Khan praises hero pilot Smit Machchhar: 'Well done bro'
item.description: Salman Khan shared his appreciation for Captain Smit Machchhar's efforts in saving lives during a flight incident. The pilot was attacked by his co-pilot while flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv and sustained serious injuries. Despite this, he managed to successfully land the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia with over 170 people on board. Other Indian celebrities, including Shilpa Shetty and Jackie Shroff, also recognized Machchhar's bravery and heroism.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: AI sings Russia's war story: Kremlin's unexpected soundtrack of Ukraine's conflict
item.description: Among the songs whose release dates could be established, most appeared after 2024. That coincided with the wider availability of AI music generators such as Sudo and Udio. It is not clear how much involvement, if any, the Russian government has had in producing or distributing the songs. However, the Kremlin has supported cultural projects aimed at promoting patriotic themes.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Oregon couple earns $100K a year from 13 wind turbines on wheat farm
item.description: In Sherman County, Oregon, a wheat-farming family thrives, thanks to the wind turbines dotting their property. These turbines not only allow for uninterrupted traditional farming practices but also generate crucial income through payments from renewable energy projects. The McCullough family's success story highlights a unique blend of agriculture and sustainable energy, benefiting not just them but also providing significant tax revenue that nurtures local services and supports rural infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Illinois farmer earns $120,000 a year from 10 wind turbines
item.description: Grain farmers across rural America are increasingly finding financial relief through payments from wind turbines placed on their land. These earnings serve as a buffer against the ups and downs of crop pricing, while also bolstering local government funding. Yet, the introduction of wind turbines is not without its challenges, as it breeds discord between farmers who benefit and those who feel left out.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Why children who sing during daily routines may be doing more than having fun
item.description: As young children engage in daily routines like dressing or eating, they often craft spontaneous songs. Such musical expressions not only showcase their creativity but also play a vital role in language development through rhythm and repetition. Parents should cherish these moments, allowing children the freedom to explore their song-making abilities without interference. Observing the themes in their melodies can reveal their interests and cognitive processes.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Gaza war could have ended a year earlier, says ex Israeli hostage negotiator
item.description: Major General Nitzan Alon revealed that the Gaza war could have been concluded a year prior. He argued that an earlier resolution would have spared the lives of countless hostages and civilians. Alon criticized the prevailing notion that total victory over Hamas had to be accomplished before any negotiations, asserting this approach was flawed.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Rajasthan Royals star creates history, surpasses Gayle for highest T20 score
item.description: Lhuan-dre Pretorius has made T20 cricket history with his phenomenal score of 188 runs off 79 balls while playing for the Titans against the Knights. This feat breaks Chris Gayle's former record of 175 runs, showcasing Pretorius's exceptional talent as he maintained a striking rate of 237.97. His recent century for South Africa further underscores his remarkable consistency and prowess on the field.

item.title: 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' scores Rs 95 crore on global debut
item.description: Ajay Devgn's 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' has achieved a significant opening at the box office. The film earned an estimated Rs 95.10 crore worldwide on its first day of release. It surpassed the opening day figures of its predecessors, 'Drishyam 2' and 'Drishyam'. Strong advance bookings contributed to the successful debut with Rs 79.71 crore in ticket sales.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Maryland homeowner gets $234,368 check for home; new law bans such offers
item.description: Effective October 1, Maryland introduced legislation banning unsolicited checks sent with home purchase offers. This initiative is designed to safeguard homeowners from misleading marketing strategies from property investors. Consumer advocates highlighted the risk of vulnerable owners being tricked into agreements upon receiving such checks. Historical precedents in consumer lending underline the necessity for legal protections, advising homeowners against accepting random financial items received through mail.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Software engineer turns childhood skill into $100-an-hour side hustle
item.description: Priyancka Jaiin reveals how her childhood love for mehndi has blossomed into a lucrative side hustle. While maintaining her career as a software engineer, she serves clients with mehndi designs for a variety of events. Her artistry not only brings joy to brides but also supports cancer patients and mothers-to-be. Emphasizing careful practice, Jaiin showcases that a simple hobby can evolve into a significant source of creativity and fulfillment.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Michael Douglas confesses to secret affair with Kathleen Turner
item.description: Michael Douglas has revealed details about his secret romantic relationship with Kathleen Turner from four decades ago. He admitted that they developed feelings for each other while filming 'Romancing the Stone'. Their relationship ended when Douglas' wife visited the set with their young son, prompting him to prioritize family. Despite the past romance, they continued to collaborate professionally on subsequent projects.
